techniques.name: Caret-tracking typewriter with accent on the newest word
techniques.description: A line types at about 2 frames a character with a solid block caret; the frame is a tight crop that follows the caret, so the start of the line exits the left edge and the caret holds near x 0.30-0.40. The word just completed is accent red for 6-7 frames, then turns to the base colour. In the interface sections a virtual camera pushes to the caret (1.4-1.8x) and the cut back to a wide shows the whole query.
techniques.routeReason: Pure type and a 2D camera over a flat field: TypedLine/typingSchedule give the characters by frame, RegionCamera follows a caret point computed from the measured text width. For the product sections the real interface must be captured (capture:app) and played under the same camera.

techniques.name: Type punch-in through a polarity flash
techniques.description: The same typed line jumps from a 11.6% to a 22-24% line box (about 1.7-2x) while the ground flips: F330-F331 white ground with the small line, F332-F333 white ground with the large line, F334 back to black. Afterwards a slow push of 8% (z 0.077) over 1.01 s, power4.out.
techniques.routeReason: Two scale states and a ground colour per frame; no new primitive beyond a scale track.

techniques.name: Polarity flip and slice-displacement glitch cut
techniques.description: Single frames flip to the opposite ground (black to white) while horizontal bands of the image are displaced sideways by 5-30% of the width; the incoming image arrives already sliced and resolves in 10-12 frames. Lengths used: 1 frame (1.92 s), 4-7 frames (word swaps), 24 frames (6.53-6.93 s, text to first person).
techniques.routeReason: Per-frame clip-path bands with seeded offsets and a ground invert are deterministic in Remotion; SliceWord covers type, a plate-level version is needed for footage.

techniques.name: Accelerating subject-swap montage under a doubling counter
techniques.description: Fixed layout: query strip at top, count right-aligned to x 0.38 at eye height, seated subject centred, plural label from x 0.61, name card below. Each cut swaps the subject and doubles the count (1 to 524 288, 20 shots). Holds 1.47, 1.53, 0.88, 0.62, 0.45, 0.45, 0.47, 0.25, 0.17, 0.15, 0.12, 0.13, 0.12, 0.10, 0.10, 0.07, 0.10, 0.03, 0.03, 0.10 s. The face cut lands 1-3 frames before the odometer roll, which takes 4-5 frames.
techniques.routeReason: Twenty different real people in the same seat and framing cannot be faked: shoot them (or license a matched set) on one locked-off camera; the counter, label and card are Remotion overlays (type-odometer-stat logic).

techniques.name: Flash frames on a subject swap: dark ghost, inverted plate, x-ray
techniques.description: For 2-4 frames the plate is replaced by a variant: the subject darkened on a near-black ground (F492-F495), a cyan skeleton x-ray on dark (F644-F647, F670-F673), or a photographic negative (F674-F675). Sometimes the subject changes under the flash (F790, F828), sometimes it stays (F644, F826).
techniques.routeReason: Colour-matrix and invert filters on the footage layer per frame are deterministic; the x-ray needs a pre-made matte or plate per subject. `grade-step-flash` step `matte` takes either `src` (x-ray artwork drawn in place of the plate, `gojiberryXrayExit`) or `matteSrc` (the plate subject's alpha cut-out, which masks the plate into a cyan negative, `gojiberryXrayFromCutout`); the repository has no local cut-out route, so the PNG is supplied or made with `pnpm rmbg` (paid, with approval).

techniques.name: Statement word: case flip letter by letter, then glyph corruption to black
techniques.description: On black, a two-word line types (second word accent for 6 frames), then glitch-swaps to a one-word answer in a slanted lower-case form. The letters flip to upright capitals one at a time, every 2-3 frames (F915-F924, 0.15 s), hold 1.2 s, then: polarity flips (F998-F1001), glyphs replaced by look-alike symbols (F1006-F1007), horizontal smear blocks (F1008-F1015), black at F1016.
techniques.routeReason: Per-glyph state per frame: Glyphs/ScrambleWord give glyph substitution, SliceWord and a ground invert give the break-up.

techniques.name: 3D brand mark glitches in at extreme close-up and pulls back with a roll
techniques.description: Glossy red extruded mark: first frames are a slice glitch of its face filling the frame (F1050-F1056), then the camera pulls back about 5.8x (z -1.76) with about 39 degrees of counter-clockwise roll over 1.4 s, ending as a speck on black that is cut at 18.5 s before the move settles.
techniques.routeReason: The library's extruded-mark block renders an SVG mark extruded in three.js inside Remotion; Blender only if a hero material is needed. The pull and roll are a camera track.

techniques.name: Pixel-mosaic ring blooms from the mark, then the wordmark types on
techniques.description: Hard cut from black to white (F1110). From the small mark a ring of coarse square pixels grows outward over about 0.7 s (F1110-F1151), leaving a warm peach gradient. The mark shrinks once (F1214) and the wordmark types on beside it at about 3 frames a letter (F1216-F1235).

techniques.name: Product demo: wide and caret close-up alternated by hard cuts
techniques.description: The real query field in the product. Close-ups on the caret (1.4-2x) while a clause types, hard cut to the wide when the clause completes so the result count and dot-matrix visual can update, then a hard cut back in for the next clause. Bracketed placeholders show the next clause in coral. Cuts at 24.6, 28.1, 30.47, 33.1 s; holds 2.4-3.5 s. Each close-up carries a short push (z 0.18-0.57).
techniques.routeReason: Captured product interface (capture:app) played in Remotion with RegionCamera keys; the cut grammar is layoutSeries.

techniques.name: Press, colour wash and ripple, result resolves out of the wash
techniques.description: The pointer presses the submit control (F2100); a pink wash (#FA9A98) rises over the interface over about 0.35 s, a ring ripples out from the pointer, and at F2122 a dot-matrix result shape appears inside the wash; the wash clears to the warm gradient by F2160 (36.0 s) with a small count that ticks down for another 0.4 s.
techniques.routeReason: Opacity of a flat colour layer, a ring scale and a crossfade between two captured states.

techniques.name: Camera tilts from the typed line down to the one matched person; badge counts to full match
techniques.description: On white the completed line drifts up and out as the camera tilts down (y 0.512 frame heights, slight pull-out z -0.22) and the seated person rises into frame (F2554-F2585). At 44.0 s a hand enters from the left with a thumbs-up (6 frames), and at F2653 a green pill grows from a dot at top centre and counts a percentage up to a full match by F2669.
techniques.routeReason: A real person and hand on a studio plate; the line and badge are Remotion overlays tracked to the tilt. If the plate is locked off, the tilt can be done in Remotion on an over-scanned frame.
